status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) extended the time limit on benefits for adults without dependents to ages 18 through 64, narrowed the child-based exemption to children under 14, removed the exemptions for veterans, people experiencing homelessness and former foster youth, and limited area waivers to unemployment of 10 percent or higher (with separate Alaska and Hawaii rules). The law also requires future Thrifty Food Plan re-evaluations to be cost neutral and limits the automatic heating and cooling utility allowance tied to energy assistance to households with an elderly or disabled member. USDA issued implementing memos in September and October 2025, and the hold-harmless period for state error rates ended 2025-11-01. A USDA draft rule to narrow broad-based categorical eligibility reached OMB on 2025-10-24, and no published proposal was found in the sources reviewed (which run through June 2026). USDA data show about 41.2 million participants in September 2025 and about 36.4 million in June 2026 (preliminary); the data do not establish the cause of the change.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed. Its SNAP sections (10101 to 10103) cap future Thrifty Food Plan increases, widen the adult work requirement and restrict waivers, and limit the utility allowance linked to energy assistance. Several provisions took effect on enactment.
FNS memo to state agencies summarizes the law's SNAP provisions: age limit raised, new exemption rules, waiver limits, cost-neutral Thrifty Food Plan adjustments, and utility allowance changes.

FNS issues guidance on the revised adult exemptions (ages 18 to 64, child exemption under 14, removal of veteran, homeless and former foster youth exemptions). USDA also announces it will end waivers granted under a provision the law repealed.
A draft USDA proposed rule titled Reforming Categorical Eligibility is received by OMB for review. No conclusion date is listed.
A federal district court in Rhode Island issues a temporary restraining order that pauses the early termination of the waivers, in a suit by eight cities and other groups.
The hold-harmless period for quality-control error rates ends; states are expected to be fully implementing the July 4 provisions.
USDA guidance reverses the early waiver terminations; the affected waivers stay in effect through their original end dates, citing the litigation.
USDA monthly data (preliminary) show about 36.4 million SNAP participants in June 2026, down from about 41.2 million in September 2025 (month-level date; exact release date not stated).

title: Tighten SNAP work requirements, categorical eligibility and utility allowances
uncertainties: Whether the categorical eligibility proposal has been published after June 2026 was not confirmed; a Federal Register search for FNS proposed and final rules since 2025-01-20 found none on categorical eligibility, and the OMB review entry is the only primary evidence. The Ballotpedia item and the NGA timeline are secondary summaries. The participation change is shown from USDA data without a causal finding; a local news article attributing it to rules effective 2026-02-01 was not verified and was not used. The shutdown-era benefit litigation and state-level implementation differences were not examined in detail. Because the Mandate proposed a regulatory path and the change came through a reconciliation law with a wider scope (ages to 64), the match is rated partial.
